tests.method: Retrieve and read primary texts defending fixed retributive desert and communicative or relational accounts of punishment; extract each account's stated ground of desert and whether later answerability changes desert or only permission to punish.
tests.pass_condition: At least one clearly formulated primary account supports a present answerability-based desert claim, and the proposal accurately identifies its conditions.
tests.fail_condition: The closest theories all make deserved punitive hardship invariant once the offense is complete, leaving only mercy or policy to explain leniency.
tests.coverage_required: Save exact retrieved source bytes, retrieval metadata, and the passages actually read; distinguish full and excerpt reading.

tests.method: Compare primary accounts of communicative punishment and restorative justice to test whether truthful public acknowledgment and feasible repair can complete accountability without imposed hardship.
tests.pass_condition: An account explains how non-punitive conduct can satisfy the relevant answerability relation while preserving condemnation and guilt.
tests.fail_condition: Punitive hardship itself is necessary to answer the wrong on every defensible account in scope.
tests.coverage_required: Record the closest passages and counterpassages actually read; do not treat a general policy preference as a desert premise.

tests.method: Use matched cases that hold fixed original culpability, elapsed time, harm, social consequences, forgiveness, and protective need while varying only independently verified accountability; ask which normative premise makes the desert claim differ.
tests.pass_condition: A non-circular premise explains the difference as a change in the ground or satisfaction condition of desert, not merely lower utility or compassion.
tests.fail_condition: The verdict can be explained only by mercy, proportionality, or institutional convenience, with no defensible internal desert difference.

tests.method: Compare self-disclosure before detection, confession after detection, continued concealment, and earlier imposition followed by later reform; include unequal resources and barriers to making repair.
tests.pass_condition: A public, conduct-based criterion distinguishes accountability from strategic evasion and gives a fair account of delayed cases without rewarding concealment.
tests.fail_condition: The exception systematically rewards evasion or depends on wealth, eloquence, disability-insensitive participation, or victim emotional labor.

tests.method: Determine whether the best account describes non-punitive accountability as satisfying the original claim, changing its object, or expiring an unfulfilled punitive claim; retain the original term only if the distinctions are defensible.
tests.pass_condition: The proposal can state exactly what expires and why it is not merely forgiveness, equivalent payment, a statute of limitations, or a discretionary bar.
tests.fail_condition: The idea's distinctive expiry claim collapses into ordinary satisfaction or an external legal/permissibility rule.

next_action: A fresh source-probe context should first test T1 and T2 against saved primary sources, then attempt T3 and T4. Do not treat this proposal as a completed essay or as literature-vetted.
